incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-9943 triggered - alert: routing-latency-p95-eu > 1.2s (3/5 hosts)
pagerduty-bot: Page fired to #eng-oncall -> @emma
emma: Acked. I'm up, looking at routing dash now.
raj: I see a cluster of synthetic canary hits in eu-west around 10:01, latency lines up.
maya: Any customer-facing errors? SLOs look steady for 5xx, this smells like canary noise.
alex: Checking edge proxies and cache layers... Redis miss-rate spiked on nodes with tag=canary.
emma: weird, this is limited to canary pool. Are CI load generators still running?
raj: Affirmative — there's a CI job that runs a stress harness, job id ci/canary/2026-03-15-10:01, spawned ~10 agents. PID list shows repeated synthetic requests.
emma: pausing that job now, will cut traffic from canaries.
emma: /tooling/ci cancel ci/canary/2026-03-15-10:01 -> done (killed 10 agents)
incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation to second level (unacked > 3m) — automated escalation triggered
emma: re-ack: I acked earlier but alert dedupe didn't group correctly; bot escalated on duplicate signals :/
maya: Confirming from dashboards: customer traffic unchanged, error budget unaffected. This is isolated to canary.
alex: After killing the loadjob, routing p95 dropped below threshold across eu nodes. Looks like a classic synthetic flood. Auto-resolve should follow.
incident-bot: Alert auto-resolved: routing-latency-p95-eu (resolved by rule)
raj: Root cause: CI canary job accidentally left with aggressive concurrency flag. It pushed canary pool over the batching threshold causing a cache miss storm.
maya: Action items: filter alerts by "tag!=canary" and tune dedupe window.
emma: Quick patch suggestion to avoid future ghosts — require non-canary traffic or larger fleet fraction. Example rule patch: 
```yaml
alert: routing_latency_p95_eu
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(route_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="router",tag!="canary"}[5m])) by (le)) > 1.0
for: 2m
```
emma: Pushed infra PR: https://git.redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/432 (adds tag filter + increases dedupe window)
alex: Nice. Also suggest updating CI job owner docs so loadjobs are labeled "no-alert" or run in isolated env.
raj: I'll follow up on the CI label change and add a quick test to ensure jobs set tag=canary explicitly.
maya: Logging this as No Customer Impact (NCI). Will add a short postmortem note to the oncall channel and update runbook.
emma: Thanks all — closing this thread, will link the postmortem when available. :white_check_mark:
